newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - MUTED AHEAD OF TAIWAN TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - MUTED AHEAD OF TAIWAN TENDER.

text.p: Gasoline was offered down but levels held steady amid crude's recovery and in lacklustre market activity as traders eyed Taiwan's import tender.
"It is a very wild card," a trader said on Taiwan's tender for 95-octane unleaded reformate for September 1-30 delivery which closes Monday and is valid for two days.
At the end of July, Taiwan cancelled its tender for September 1-15 due to high offers of around $25.30 per barrel, c+f.
Since then, fob Singapore 95-octane prices have fallen by more than a dollar from $23.80.
On Monday, a Swiss trader offered at $22.60 for September 6-10 lifting, shaving off 30 cents from his Friday offer.
But some traders said the offer was too low as 92-octane was bid just 15 cents lower at $22.45.
"Fifteen cents is just ridiculous," a trader said.

A more realistic number for the 95-octane was around $23.50, placing the grade $1.40 lower than 97-octane and $1.00 above 92-octane, reflecting the two-tiered market of the tight high-octane and well-supplied low octane, a trader said.

"If the market takes the seller's number, it would place offers into Taiwan to be as low as $23.60 after adding freight," the trader said. "I don't see how you can make the numbers unless you are desperate."
Naphtha September swaps lost a marginal 5-10 cents per barrel, with quotes last cited at $21.20/$21.30.
Stocks in Asia remained high with India adding to the surplus with two new HAN export tenders.
The first offered 25,000 tonnes lifting from Bombay on the west coast between August 31-September 2 and closes August 13 and is valid for a day.
The second is for 30,000 tonnes from Cochin on the east coast, lifting September 8-10 and closes August 21 and is valid for a day.

Reflecting the soft market, India sold its second August Madras LAN cargo by tender to South Korea's Hanwha Chemical Corp at around $20 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob, lower than its last August 6-8 Madras LAN award at a $19 discount.
